newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE July coffee hits new one-year high at $1,849.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE July coffee hits new one-year high at $1,849.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures hit a new one-year high of $1,849 a tonne, up $32, on Wednesday as the market extended its dazzling rally that began in early January.

Traders said the buying, led by funds and roasters, was powered by the unabated run-up in New York arabica futures on Tuesday. July arabica futures surged to the highest level since July 1994 when frosts hit Brazilian crop.
By 0950 GMT, LIFFE's July rose further to trade at $1,850, up $33.
New York's July ended 11.50 cents at 241.15 cents a lb after a new peak at 243.00 cents.

The market's bullish tone was supported by long-term weather forecasts calling for a cool air mass to push across Argentina and and into Brazil in eight to 10 days. With producer and consumer stocks at low levels, traders and roasters would be incredibly sensitive to any frost threat over the next 15 weeks, broker GNI said.

"There are bound to be at least two serious (frost) scares during the season, and no one would want to get short with the realistic prospect of $5 to $7 coffee if 1994 damage was repeated," it added. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
